chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Blue Vein Society and being kept out of private dances
summary: Milt describes the Blue Vein Society in Vicksburg; Danny remembers his mother saying private dances would not let them in. End of tape 1 side A.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In Vicksburg, Mississippi, we had Blue Vein Society...

...where they could see if you're light enough for them to see your veins. If they could see the blue blood through your veins, then you could come to their (?), but a guy like me, I didn't have a chance!
Well, you have your own thing. It was like the blue bloods.
No. We would let them have it.

You know, so that is the strata. So as a kid in New Orleans, you went through all of that. "Oh, they have a dance at the Jeunes(?) Ami(?) all night. I think I'll go. I heard they've got a dance." You wanted to go to

everything, because you'd want to hear the bands, when you could (?) with this band. My mother would say, "You don't want to go there. Those people aren't to let you in there. That's a private affair."
